evidence: Cic. Verr. 2.1.133: columnam quae ad perpendiculum esse possit
Cato Agr. 20: rēctam stāre oportet in mediō ad perpendiculum
terms.comment: Latin says “vertical” with the plumb line, perpendiculum (see “plumb bob”): what stands ad perpendiculum hangs as the plumb line hangs. The adjective perpendiculāris is late (Front. Expos. Form., Lewis & Short).

evidence: Caes. B.C. 1.45: praeruptus locus utrāque ex parte dīrēctus (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: straight, whether horizontally or perpendicularly; of a cliff, sheer. Also spelt dērēctus.

phrases.latin: Līneam ab summō ad īmum ad perpendiculum dūc, nōn oblīquam.
phrases.english: Draw a line from top to bottom, straight up and down, not slanting.

phrases.latin: dīcunt eī ferē nūllam esse columnam quae ad perpendiculum esse possit
phrases.english: they tell him there is hardly a column that can be truly vertical

phrases.latin: Columellam ferream, quae in mīliāriō stat, eam rēctam stāre oportet in mediō ad perpendiculum
phrases.english: The iron pin that stands in the central pillar must stand straight in the middle, plumb

sources: Lewis & Short: perpendiculum · Lewis & Short: erigo · Lewis & Short: dirigo · Lewis & Short: perpendicularis
